forecaster_note: "There's a downward swell trend so make the most of this morning window. NE windswell will be leaving it a little lumpy but there should still be some fun waves about. Stomach to chest high for most breaks, and looking the best once the tide starts coming in. Light NNW winds and clean conditions for the Nth corners/Sth facing beaches then more lumpy and onshore later in the day as NNE winds pick up." — Max Stanley-Jones, Surfline. Agent read: 54 kJ at 10am is the best number you'll see for four days, and the 61° ENE angle sits right in Dee Why's window. Friday backs off to 37 kJ but goes clean NW offshore all day; Saturday is the flattest day on the chart at 10–19 kJ; Sunday rebuilds to 65 kJ, though the bulk of it arrives from 185° — dead south, which wraps badly into Dee Why.

wind.summary: Light NW offshore at dawn, swinging N by 10am and NE onshore 17 gusting 31 kph by mid-afternoon

shark.summary: SharkSmart NSW feed is reachable but its newest notification is dated 18 Aug (~46 hours old), so an empty last-24h window means the feed isn't refreshing — not that the water is verified clear. Most recent Northern Beaches shark sightings on record: Mona Vale and Newport, both 15 Aug (water evacuated). Tap to check live detections before you paddle out.

days.label: Today
days.note: Go early. 54 kJ of ENE windswell peaking around 10am with light NW offshore at dawn, but the wind swings N by 10 and NE onshore 17 gusting 31 kph through the afternoon — Surfline drops the rating from Fair to Poor-Fair at 10am for that reason. Low tide 6:49am filling to a 1.35m high at 1:50pm, so it improves as the tide pushes.

dee-why.window: 6:45–9:30am. NW offshore off the 6:49am low, tide pushing in. Rating drops to Poor-Fair from 10am when the wind goes N then NE.

tip.label: Frontside at the Point
tip.text: 61° is dead centre of your good window here — nothing like the dead-south rubbish coming Sunday. It's only 6-second period though, so the sets stack up fast and short: sit tighter to the Point than you would on a groundswell and take the first one of each set before the wind gets at it.

long-reef.window: Dawn–midday. Holds Fair all day here — the only one of the four Surfline doesn't downgrade at 10am, and the wind stays offshore-to-cross an extra two hours.

tip.label: Pick of the four today
tip.text: Same 54 kJ as everywhere else but a full foot bigger, and it's the only spot that keeps a Fair rating right through the NE change. If you want the punchy waist-to-shoulder session on this ENE angle, take the extra paddle.

curl-curl.window: 6:45–11:00am. Offshore holds until roughly noon, then NNE crosses it up.

tip.label: Punchy beachie option
tip.text: This is the punchy 3–4ft beachie you rate, and Surfline holds it Fair all day. Short-period ENE into open beach means shifting peaks — pick a bank at first light and stay on it rather than chasing peaks once the N wind arrives.

manly.window: Dawn only — cross-shore from 8am and Poor-Fair from 10.
alerts: Wind goes cross at North Steyne two hours before the northern spots

tip.label: Skip unless you're already south
tip.text: Same energy, worst exposure. North Steyne is the first of the four to lose the offshore and the smallest on this angle — Dee Why or Long Reef is a better use of the same drive.

days.label: Tomorrow
days.note: Energy eases 54 → 37 kJ, but the wind is the story: NW offshore from dawn to dark, only turning nasty (20 gusting 40 kph) by mid-afternoon. Small, clean, and worth a mid-morning session. Low 7:39am, high 2:56pm.

dee-why.window: 8:00–11:00am. Clean NW offshore before it builds to 20 gusting 40 kph by 3pm.
alerts: Energy drops to 25 kJ by late afternoon

long-reef.window: Mid-morning. Biggest of the four again and holds Fair until mid-afternoon.

days.label: Weekend
days.note: Saturday is the flattest day on the chart — 10–19 kJ, shin-to-knee, not worth the drive. Sunday is the weekend session: 65 kJ by mid-morning with light W/WSW offshore until about 11am. The catch is the primary swell — 2.8ft at 10s from 185°, dead south, which wraps badly into Dee Why. Long Reef and Curl Curl handle that angle far better.

dee-why.window: Sunday 8:00–11:00am only. Saturday is a write-off.
alerts: Sun 23: 185° primary is dead south and wraps poorly here

long-reef.window: Sunday 8:00–11:30am — best of the four on the S angle and the only one at chest high.

curl-curl.window: Sunday morning. W offshore until roughly 11am, NE crosses it by mid-afternoon.

manly.window: Sunday 8:00–10:00am. Rated Fair early but the smallest of the four.
alerts: Weakest of the four across both days
